sizing.note: Above the 6-file heuristic, but NOT split: this is one non-decomposable feature (KML import). The file count is driven by Dalton's grooming choices (support holes + queue large files) plus test files. Parser->importer->job/action->resource wiring are a single deliverable and cannot ship independently. Built as ONE implementation node because the interfaces (parser output shape -> importer signature -> job/action call sites) must co-evolve; splitting across blind parallel workers would produce interface mismatches.

async_feedback_decision: Queued-path completion feedback = an EMAIL notification (App\Notifications\ZoneImportCompleted) via the Notifiable User. Chosen over enabling Filament's panel-wide database-notification bell (which app/Providers/Filament panels do NOT currently enable) to keep the change self-contained and avoid a cross-cutting admin-UI change. Assumption flagged for Dalton at QA/handoff; switching to an in-app bell later is a light-path change.

subtasks.title: KML bulk-import for Zone Manager (parser + shared importer + queued job + Filament action + toolbar wiring)
subtasks.approach: Build the whole feature in ONE node via TDD, in dependency order, reusing the existing Zone geometry pipeline. Order: (1) ScoutAnalyticsEvent::ZoneImport enum case. (2) KmlZoneParser service (TDD parser test first): namespace-aware SimpleXML (registerXPathNamespace 'kml' => http://www.opengis.net/kml/2.2, xpath //kml:Placemark), read <name> (fallback 'Imported Zone {n}'), parse <Polygon><outerBoundaryIs><LinearRing><coordinates> as outer ring + each <innerBoundaryIs><LinearRing><coordinates> as a hole, strip altitude (3rd tuple element), force-close each ring, validate EACH ring (>=4 positions & closed) replicating Zone::geoJsonHasValidRing's threshold; invalid outer => skip placemark (record reason), invalid hole => drop that hole keep the polygon; emit GeoJSON Polygon coordinates=[outer, ...holes]; non-<Polygon> placemarks skipped+counted; never let a SimpleXML libxml warning/exception escape (libxml_use_internal_errors). (3) ZoneKmlImporter service: run(string $kml, int $orgId, int $userId): array{created:int,skipped:int,skip_reasons:array} — calls the parser, per valid polygon wraps Zone::create([org_id,created_by_user_id,name,color=Zone::DEFAULT_COLOR,is_no_scan_zone=false,definition=['polygons'=>[$polygon],'zip_codes'=>[]]]) + $zone->rebuildGeometryFromDefinition() in its OWN DB::connection('platform')->transaction()+try/catch (per-placemark, NOT one wrapping txn), tallies counts, fires ONE Analytics::track(ScoutAnalyticsEvent::ZoneImport, user, ['created'=>N,'skipped'=>M], ScoutAnalyticsPage::Zones). Written ONCE, called by both the sync action and the job. (4) ImportZonesFromKml job (ShouldQueue): ctor(string $storedPath, string $disk, int $orgId, int $userId); handle() reads the stored KML from the disk, calls ZoneKmlImporter::run(), notifies the user by email (ZoneImportCompleted) with the counts, deletes the stored file in a finally; failed() emails a failure notice + deletes the file. (5) App\Notifications\ZoneImportCompleted (queued mail notification): 'Your KML zone import finished — N created, M skipped' (+ a failure state). (6) ZoneKmlImportAction static action: schema() = required FileUpload('file') with acceptedFileTypes(['application/vnd.google-earth.kml+xml','text/xml','application/xml','application/octet-stream']) + ->rules(['mimes:kml']) (extension backstop; verify empirically) + ->maxSize(config value); action() = Gate::authorize('create', Zone::class) once, then decide sync-vs-queue by a named threshold (default: raw file size > ZoneKmlImportAction::QUEUE_THRESHOLD_BYTES ~ 262144). SYNC: read TemporaryUploadedFile->get(), ZoneKmlImporter::run() inline, immediate summary Notification ('Imported N zones, skipped M'). QUEUE: persist the upload to a private disk, dispatch ImportZonesFromKml, show 'Import started — you'll be emailed when it finishes'. (7) Wire ZoneKmlImportAction::make() into ZoneResource::table()->toolbarActions([...]) beside 'create', ->visible(fn(): bool => static::canCreate()). Then the Filament action/resource test + job test. Run pint + full suite at the end.
subtasks.intended_diffs: See approach — per-file: enum(+1 case), 2 new services, 1 job, 1 notification, 1 action, ZoneResource(+1 toolbar entry using the existing canCreate() gate), 3 test files (parser unit incl. a holed polygon; job unit incl. email + cleanup; Filament action/resource test incl. gating parity + sync happy-path + partial-skip + org isolation + large-file dispatch via Bus::fake).
